concept.name: Kijun-sen
concept.definition: The slower Ichimoku line: the midpoint of the 26-period high-low range, serving as the medium-term equilibrium level, signal-confirmation line, and a common trailing reference.
concept.intuition: It marks the recent balance point of the market; price far above it is extended, and pullbacks to a flat Kijun are watched as equilibrium tests.
concept.mechanics: Compute (max(High,26) + min(Low,26))/2 each bar. Price-Kijun crosses and Tenkan-Kijun crosses generate Ichimoku momentum signals, while the Kijun's slope and flatness gauge the medium-term trend.
concept.failure_modes: Stepwise movement and lag; in ranges price crosses it repeatedly with no follow-through.
concept.misconceptions: A touch of the Kijun is not automatically support - it is only the midpoint of the last 26 bars' range.
concept.example: With a 26-bar high of 110 and low of 96, Kijun-sen = 103.
